items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: If George Gershwin were alive and he could sue you for stealing chord changes, I would be in jail just like Dizzy Gillespie would be in jail.

ctx.x: Okay. Well speaking of ideas, you wrote that when you first tried to play bebop early on that your first note and your last note would be right, and everything in the middle was very questionable.

Well you’ve got to understand, when I first heard Bird and Diz I was home on furlough. And when I heard — I didn’t believe what I was hearing. But I know they were playing double-time, and I was in the Army by the way, I was on furlough. And in the Army I was the drummer with a 38-piece orchestra making all the Army movie pictures. We had a number of drummers in the band so we used to have little jam sessions and I would play vibes, with some of the other drummers playing. And I played straight ahead, you know.…

be George Gershwin. Because everything he played was a song. Everything that came out of that horn, you slow it down and you could write a lyric to it. So my point, getting back to that first note, I heard all those notes so I wanted to play them but I didn’t know what the heck they were doing, so I said the first note I hit was always boom — and I ended up on saying boom. In the middle is [inaudible]. The rhythms were there but not the notes until I came out of the Army and started jamming with players who were…
